analysis.title: GS - Pasquariello - markets macro - 23 Oct 2026
key_insights: S&P 500 has been range-bound for three months. 60-day realized volatility is about 10%, in the bottom quartile of the COVID and post-COVID era.
The S&P moved only 47 bps this week, but the GS hedge fund VIP pair trade was hit again. Pasquariello says the market has hammered consensus positions, part positioning and part fundamental.

Hedge fund performance has drawn down since the end of June after a strong first half that included an exceptional Q2. Allocators carried heavy length in the AI theme, which has now retraced significantly.

GS franchise flows showed consistent de-risking in both net and gross exposure over recent weeks. Pasquariello says the market 'cut into some bone' this week. Thursday saw the most tech selling of any day in the past two years (GS PB).

Fundamental skepticism has entered the AI narrative. Mega cap execution and demand look intact, but the market is questioning supply of power and capital as forward spending commitments pile up. This creates uncertainty about the path and sequence of the AI buildout.
Oil broke out this week. Midterm elections are increasingly raised in client conversations, with a negative skew.
Pasquariello's risk/reward view is unchanged from a few weeks ago: unclear. He has limited conviction and is comfortable 'swimming closer to shore'.

Historically, when he voices this kind of caution, risk/reward has already improved toward the bull. The past month brought heavy de-risking among levered investors, firmer implied volatility, a hard hit to cyclicals vs defensives, and the first negative reading of the GS Risk Appetite Indicator since March.
Hyperscaler earnings next week are the key catalyst. GS S&P EPS growth estimates (ex-PE) are +29% in 2026, +18% in 2027 and +11% in 2028.
Pasquariello expects the primary trend to stay higher but with a flatter gradient: the bull market continues but with less punch and more volatility.

Corporate credit price action has been ugly and not limited to AI. Credit contacts described conditions as 'melting down' more than once. The weekly podcast covers credit with chief credit strategist Amanda Lynam.
A GS chart of AI leaders vs S&P ex-AI shows the ex-AI index on track for its best single month in three years, even as AI leaders have fallen sharply. Positioning explains part of the divergence.

sector_views.rationale: Mega caps keep executing and demand is intact, but power and capital constraints raise questions on the AI buildout. Tech selling on Thursday was the heaviest in two years.
Cyclicals vs defensives has been hit hard over the past month, which Pasquariello cites as a sign the market has done 'a lot of work'.

tension_points.bull_case: The market has done a lot of work: heavy levered de-risking, firmer implied volatility, cyclicals vs defensives hit hard, and a negative Risk Appetite Indicator for the first time since March. Wall-of-worry logic suggests odds may favor the bull. GS sees +18% EPS growth in 2027, and bear markets with double-digit EPS growth are rare.
tension_points.bear_case: Pressures keep accumulating: energy prices, sovereign stress, midterms, AI power and capital constraints and ugly credit. Slowing EPS growth leaves less offset to macro headwinds, and the market may be complacent.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A miss on the +18% 2027 EPS growth estimate would undermine the view that the primary trend stays higher.

theme_stances.key_argument: The market is asking hard questions about the supply of power and capital needed for the AI buildout, raising uncertainty about its path and sequence.
theme_stances.evidence: the two variables that stand out right now are POWER and CAPITAL

theme_stances.key_argument: After months of range trading, Pasquariello has limited conviction and prefers to stay closer to shore, though prior similar caution has preceded better odds for bulls.
theme_stances.evidence: I have no issue with swimming a bit closer to shore right now
